cards.text: Chronicles has been walking through the families of Israel, the man once called Jacob (Genesis 32:28), one son at a time (1 Chronicles 2-4), and now it's Reuben's turn. Reuben is the firstborn, so the birthright should be his. But Chronicles stops RIGHT away to say it went to somebody else.

cards.question: Reuben is Israel's firstborn. So who does his birthright go to?

cards.text: Chronicles gives the reason plainly: Reuben defiled his father's bed.

cards.question: After what Reuben did, Chronicles still counts him by birthright.

cards.text: Joseph, son of Israel, holds the birthright, but Judah, another son of Israel (Genesis 35:23), prevails over his brothers. No birthright and STILL on top, while I spent years at the bottom of a junk drawer under a pile of takeout menus.

cards.question: From Judah came a ___, even though the birthright belonged to Joseph.

cards.text: Then come Reuben's sons, Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron and Carmi, and a family line from a man named Joel down to Beerah, a Reubenite leader. Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria carries Beerah into exile. Beerah's relatives settle in Aroer and as far as Nebo and Baal-meon.

cards.question: The Reubenites also spread east to the edge of the desert that stretches to the Euphrates River, because their ___ had increased in the land of Gilead.

cards.text: In the days of Saul, king of Israel (1 Samuel 11:15), the Reubenites go to war against a people called the Hagrites.

cards.question: In the days of Saul, the Reubenites lose their war with the Hagrites.

cards.text: Next door, in Bashan, live the descendants of Gad, another son of Israel (Genesis 35:26), and Chronicles lists their chiefs and family heads. They live in Gilead, in Bashan and its towns, and throughout the pasturelands of Sharon, all recorded in the days of Jotham king of Judah and Jeroboam king of Israel.

Now Chronicles zooms out: Reuben, Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh, named for one of Joseph's sons (Genesis 41:51), have 44,760 warriors trained for battle. They go to war against the Hagrites, as well as Jetur, Naphish and Nodab.

cards.question: What do Reuben, Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh do in the middle of the battle against the Hagrites?

answers.text: They call to Judah for help

cards.text: God answers their prayers because they put their trust in Him, and the Hagrites and all their allies are delivered into their hands. They seize 50,000 camels, 250,000 sheep and 2,000 donkeys, and take 100,000 captives.

cards.question: Many others fell slain in the war against the Hagrites, because the battle belonged to ___.

cards.text: Reuben, Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh occupy that land until the exile. The half-tribe of Manasseh is numerous, settled from Bashan to Baal-hermon, also known as Mount Hermon, and that is a LOT of cousins for one group chat. Chronicles names their family heads: mighty men of valor, famous men.

cards.question: Manasseh's family heads were mighty, famous men. But what does Chronicles say went wrong?
The unfaithfulness Chronicles describes is turning to the gods of the peoples of the land, peoples God had destroyed before them.

cards.text: So Pul king of Assyria, also called Tiglath-pileser, the same king who carried Beerah into exile, takes Reuben, Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh into exile. He brings them to Halah, Habor, Hara and the river of Gozan, and the writer says they're still there to this day.

cards.question: Who stirred up the spirit of Pul king of Assyria to carry Reuben, Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh into exile?
